result.rationale: The diff adds `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts. Relying on statusText for success checking is a real defect: Node's undici fetch returns an empty statusText regardless of status code (and reason phrases are locale/implementation dependent), so successful 200 token refreshes would throw. This check was newly introduced in this diff, so the broken behavior is introduced here.

judged_text: The refresh response check uses `response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is locale-dependent and empty for HTTP/2 fetch responses. On Node fetch (undici), statusText for a 200 HTTP/2 response is often an empty string, so every Salesforce refresh throws HttpError 400 even though the token was successfully issued; users on any deployment using HTTP/2 or non-English reason phrases get a broken Salesforce integration.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh flow checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. `statusText` is not a reliable success indicator (it can vary by server/reason phrase and may be empty), so a successful 200 response can incorrectly throw. This is a functional defect introduced by the diff; it should use `response.ok` or `response.status` instead.
